objections.claim: The spec's Step 9 procedure and its writer mode table together leave the dialogue loop's rebuttal→judge→OVERTURN admit path structurally unable to merge. On admit, the last recorded round is the reviewer pass that raised the critical — its signal is `fail` or `needs-human`, never `pass` (the reviewer flagged the finding; it is the judge that later overturns it). Graft Step 9 step 5 writes only when the terminal signal is `pass` or `needs-human`; the judge not-admit arm parks, and the admit arm proceeds straight to Step 9b with no terminal write specified. If no write fires, `review-verdict.json` is missing and the anchor mint refuses `floor-incomplete` — the admitted build parks. If the builder instead reaches for `--park needs-human`, the file carries a non-pass signal and `readReviewVerdict` refuses the merge leg. And the default mode cannot be forced either: it exits 1 on a `fail` terminal round ("the review loop has not finished"), and no mode derives `signal: pass` from a judge verdict — the recorder refuses synthetic rounds and the park write "never adds a synthetic round". Every write mode the spec defines dead-ends the one terminal state the dialogue loop exists to reach.
objections.evidence: "Writer modes for `review-verdict`" table (default mode precondition "terminal round signal `pass` or `needs-human`"; error "terminal round is fail; the review loop has not finished"); `graft_step_9_pass` step 5 ("IF signal in {pass, needs-human} and this is the terminal verdict"); the park-arm list ("The hold-limit park and the judge not-admit park run `--park needs-human`") which names every park but no admit-path write; "a park write never adds a synthetic round".
objections.predicted_consequence: every autonomous build whose critical is resolved by judge overturn rather than by a fix-path pass parks at the anchor mint (`floor-incomplete`) or is refused at merge (`review-verdict.json` signal ≠ pass) — the dialogue loop's success outcome can never ship without a spec change.
objections.disposition_rationale: Added a --judge-admitted writer mode: signal pass plus admitted_by "build-judge", checked against build-review/judge/admit-result.json; the overturned finding keeps its recorded disposition. Inside the dialogue loop no pass is terminal; the loop outcome writes once (admit, not-admit or hold-limit).

objections.claim: The spec has the recorder resolve ids with `resolveRoundChain` and store `finding_id` (step 6 of `record_review_round`), then has the collator *re-resolve* ids from stored `carried_id`/`title`/`location` with every stored `finding_id` removed (collation step 0). These two resolutions are not guaranteed to agree. The recorder resolves over the contiguous run ending at the new round *including* the new round's findings; the collator resolves over the same run but with the new round's `finding_id` removed. For a titled finding, `readerFindingIds` computes the id from title/location, so removal is a no-op and the ids agree. But for an *untitled* finding, `readerFindingIds` falls back to the stored `finding_id` — which the recorder just wrote — and the collator removes it, so the collator's fallback is `round-<n>#<i>`, a different id. The spec's own DONE item acknowledges this ("a stored `finding_id` edited after recording does not change the merge, including for an untitled finding whose carry is refused on re-resolution") but only tests the *edited* case; the unedited case is the same divergence. The merged finding's `finding_id` in `review-verdict.json` is therefore the collator's id, which for an untitled finding differs from the id the recorder stored in the round record — and the round record is what FAFF-1276's readers and the dialogue-loop churn/judge readers consume. Two consumers of the same run dir see different ids for the same finding.
objections.evidence: FAFF-1268 spec, "Round record" step 6 ("ids = resolveRoundChain(...)[last]; finding_id = ids[i].id") vs. "Collation" step 0 ("resolveRoundChain(run) with ... every finding's stored finding_id removed first"); `finding-id.js` `readerFindingIds` ("if (titled[i]) return findingId(...); return storedFindingId(f) || roundScopedId(round, i)").
objections.predicted_consequence: A finding with no title (the schema allows `title: null`) is recorded with id `round-<n>#<i>` (the recorder's resolution, which sees the stored id it just wrote) and collated with id `round-<n>#<i>` only if the collator's resolution happens to agree — but the collator removed the stored id, so it falls back to `round-<n>#<i>` too, which *is* the same id. The divergence is narrower than claimed: the recorder's `resolveRoundChain` call happens *before* the `finding_id` is written (step 6 computes ids, step 9 writes the file), so the recorder's resolution also sees no stored id for the new round. The two resolutions agree. This objection does not survive scrutiny — the recorder resolves the new round's findings before storing their ids, so the collator's removal is a no-op for the new round, and for prior rounds both see the stored ids identically. Downgrade to observation.
objections.disposition_rationale: Checked against the spec: record_review_round ignores a supplied finding_id and removes every finding_id before calling resolveRoundChain (steps 5 and 6), and the collator removes them too, so both resolve from identical inputs. objections.claim: The spec records dialogue-loop passes with `--no-carry` (every `carried_id` null), so their ids fall back to the FAFF-1266 title rule. But the dialogue loop's own churn reader (`faff build-review-churn`, FAFF-1276) resolves ids over `build-review/`'s records *with* carries. objections.claim: The writer mode `--judge-admitted` grants `signal: "pass"` (plus `admitted_by: "build-judge"`) after corroborating only that `<issue-dir>/build-review/judge/admit-result.json` parses with `admit: true`. That file lives inside the run dir, which the spec itself declares build-agent-writable ("round records sit in a run dir the build agent can write"), and the judge's mode-0600 files are written by the same user the build agent runs as — the permission bit constrains other users, not the author. The author agent therefore has a one-command fail-open path: write `{"admit": true}` to `admit-result.json`, run `faff evidence write review-verdict --judge-admitted`, and a `needs-human` terminal round with a standing critical becomes a merge-gate-passing `review-verdict.json`. The spec's stated safeguard — "the writer corroborates the admit from the judge's own `admit-result.json` … rather than taking graft's word" — is not a control at all: graft's word and the corroborating file have the same writer. The spec never establishes who can write `admit-result.json` or that it is tamper-evident, yet it grants merge-gate authority on its contents. This contradicts the spec's own design principle ("A file never claims a settlement the review did not reach") and its own anti-pattern that the author agent must never vouch for itself (the FAFF-1276 anti-pattern against an author choosing carries exists for exactly this incentive).

objections.claim: The spec routes a recorder exit 1 ("treat as a malformed reviewer block (existing needs-human path)") to `--park needs-human`, but that mode requires at least one round and exits 1 with none. On the first pass — exactly when a malformed block is most likely — no round exists, so the park write fails, no `review-verdict.json` is written, and the reviewer's raw findings vanish from the evidence trail. This is a regression the spec causes: today the park hand-writes the raw block (the very hand-write this slice removes), and the spec forbids restoring it ("no longer ... hand-writes `review-verdict.json`"). The asymmetry with `--park unavailable` (explicitly allowed zero rounds, `rounds_total: 0`) is unexplained.

objections.predicted_consequence: A first-pass malformed reviewer block parks with no `review-verdict.json` at all; the findings survive only in the mutable graft log and the park comment, and the "nothing a reviewer raised is lost" design principle is violated on this path.
objections.disposition_rationale: --park needs-human now allows zero rounds and writes rounds_total 0 and findings [], matching --park unavailable; the unrecorded block stays in the graft log. DONE covers both park modes with no rounds.
